info.name: Tokri API — Blinket-like app (all roles)
info.description:
**Server:** `http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1`

## Folders = roles

Every request name starts with the role that may call it, e.g. `[VENDOR] Create a product`.

| Folder | Who |
|---|---|
| 00 · 🔑 Sign in (run first) | Anyone — returns the token for one role |
| 01 · 👑 SUPER ADMIN | Super Admin only |
| 02 · 🛡️ ADMIN | Admin or Super Admin |
| 03 · 🏪 VENDOR (store owner + staff) | Vendor (store owner), or store staff whose permissions allow it |
| 04 · 🛵 RIDER (delivery partner) | Rider / delivery partner |
| 05 · 🛒 CUSTOMER | Customer |
| 06 · 🌐 PUBLIC (no login) | Anyone — no token needed |
| 07 · 👤 ANY LOGGED-IN USER | Any signed-in role |

**Passwords are not stored here.** Set `superAdminPassword`, `adminPassword`, … as the *Current value* only (never the Initial value — this workspace is public).

# Tokri API

Multi-vendor grocery delivery. Every endpoint the service exposes, grouped
by **who is allowed to call it**.

## Start here

Open **00 · Sign in** and run the login for the role you want. Each one
saves its token into a collection variable, so the folders below work
immediately afterwards — no copying JWTs by hand.

## How authorisation works

The API is **deny by default**. A global guard chain runs on every request:

```
ThrottlerGuard -> JwtAuthGuard -> RolesGuard -> VendorScopeGuard -> ResourceOwnerGuard
```

A route is only reachable without a token if it is explicitly marked
`@Public()`, and there are 20 of those out of 206.

`VendorScopeGuard` is worth calling out: a vendor cannot reach another
vendor's data by changing an id in the URL. The scope comes from the token,
never from the request.

## Conventions

* **Money is always INTEGER PAISE.** ₹429 is `42900`.
* **Lists paginate** with `?page=&limit=` and answer
  `{ data, meta: { page, limit, total, pages } }`.
* **Errors are RFC 7807** problem documents, with a machine-readable
  `errors.code` where one exists.
* **Validation is strict.** An unknown query parameter or body field is a
  `400`, never a silent ignore.

request.description:
**👤 Role:** Super Admin only

**URL:** `GET http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/admin/payments`

---

Payment list (paginated, SUPER_ADMIN only)

One row per order: `Order.payment` flattened onto it. Filters: q (order no, gateway ref, customer or store name), method, status, and from/to on `placedAt` (a bare YYYY-MM-DD `to` includes that whole UTC day). All money is INTEGER PAISE.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`

item.name: [SUPER ADMIN] Refund a collected payment (SUPER_ADMIN only)

request.description:
**👤 Role:** Super Admin only

**URL:** `POST http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/admin/payments/{id}/refund`

---

Refund a collected payment (SUPER_ADMIN only)

`:id` is the order id. Online: the gateway must accept the refund first — 503 `PAYMENT_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED` while Razorpay has no keys, and nothing is written. COD: recorded against the vendor ledger; the cash goes back out of band. Returns the updated row.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`, `409`, `503`

item.name: [SUPER ADMIN] Run one report over a window (SUPER_ADMIN only)

query.description: Inclusive start, ISO-8601. Defaults to 30 days ago.
Inclusive end, ISO-8601. Defaults to now.
Must be one the chosen report supports; defaults to its first. sales: day|week|month · vendor_performance: vendor · product_performance: aisle · delivery_performance: day · tax_summary: slab.

request.description:
**👤 Role:** Super Admin only

**URL:** `GET http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/admin/reports`

---

Run one report over a window (SUPER_ADMIN only)

`report` picks the read model; `grouping` must be one it supports. Rows are sparse (no row for an empty bucket) and answer in the usual `{ data, meta }` envelope, unpaged. Money is INTEGER PAISE, percentages are 0–100, and `null` means "not measurable for this row" — never zero. Buckets are UTC days.

Row keys — sales: date, orders, gmvPaise, aovPaise, discountPaise, commissionPaise · vendor_performance: vendorId, vendor, city, orders, gmvPaise, commissionPaise, cancelPct · product_performance: aisleKey, products, units, gmvPaise, sharePct · delivery_performance: date, deliveries, avgMinutes, onTimePct, failed · tax_summary: slab, orders, taxablePaise, taxPaise.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`

**👤 Role:** Super Admin only

**URL:** `POST http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/admin/riders/{id}/wallet/credit`

---

Credit a rider wallet (SUPER_ADMIN)

How a rider actually gets money while there is no payment gateway. Written as an ADJUSTMENT with `createdBy` set — NOT as a TOPUP, which would corrupt `lifetimeToppedUpPaise`, a figure somebody will reconcile against gateway settlements. Audited, and the note is mandatory.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `201`, `404`

**👤 Role:** Super Admin only

**URL:** `PUT http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/admin/settings`

---

Update platform settings (SUPER_ADMIN only)

Merge semantics: an omitted key keeps its current value. Each key is upserted individually so two admins editing different fields do not clobber one another. Every change is audited with a diff of only the keys that moved.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`

item.name: [SUPER ADMIN] Generate settlements for a period (SUPER_ADMIN only)

request.description:
**👤 Role:** Super Admin only

**URL:** `POST http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/admin/settlements/generate`

---

Generate settlements for a period (SUPER_ADMIN only)

Rolls DELIVERED orders in the window into one Settlement per vendor and reconciles the LedgerEntry rows. Safe to run twice: { vendorId, periodStart, periodEnd } is unique, so a repeat run reports the vendor under `skipped` instead of paying the week out again.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `201`, `403`

item.name: [SUPER ADMIN] Mark a settlement paid (SUPER_ADMIN only)

request.description:
**👤 Role:** Super Admin only

**URL:** `POST http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/admin/settlements/{id}/pay`

---

Mark a settlement paid (SUPER_ADMIN only)

Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header: a retried request replays the original response rather than writing a second payout row. An already-paid settlement is a 409 regardless of the key.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`, `409`

**👤 Role:** Super Admin only

**URL:** `POST http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/admin/team`

---

Create an ADMIN

The role is fixed to ADMIN by the service and is not a field on the body. A SUPER_ADMIN can NEVER be created through the API — the only one is provisioned by the seed script from `.env`.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `201`, `409`

**👤 Role:** Super Admin only

**URL:** `DELETE http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/admin/team/{id}`

---

Delete a team member

Suspension is the normal action. Refused for your own account and for seeded system accounts, which are the break-glass identities.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `204`, `403`

**URL:** `POST http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/delivery/profile/kyc`

---

Submit Aadhaar, PAN and driving licence (and the vehicle)

Sets status SUBMITTED and stamps `kycSlaDueAt = now + RIDER_KYC_SLA_HOURS`. Formats are validated at the edge — a typo must not consume a human's 24-hour SLA. A rider may resubmit while NOT_STARTED, SUBMITTED or REJECTED; a VERIFIED record is 409, because silently replacing an identity a human approved would make the approval meaningless.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `delivery`.

**Responses** — `200`, `400`, `403`, `409`

**👤 Role:** Rider / delivery partner

**URL:** `PUT http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/delivery/profile/kyc/vehicle`

---

Update the vehicle: plate, RC, insurance policy and expiry

The one part of KYC a VERIFIED rider may change themselves — vehicles are replaced and insurance renews every year. A CHANGE to a verified record sends it back to SUBMITTED with a fresh SLA, because no human has seen the new details; resending what is already on file changes nothing. While SUBMITTED the deadline does not move; a REJECTED record is resubmitted. 409 before any identity has been submitted. An expired policy is accepted and flagged.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `delivery`.

**Responses** — `200`, `400`, `403`, `409`

request.description:
**👤 Role:** Rider / delivery partner

**URL:** `GET http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/delivery/profile/kyc`

---

Verification status, masked numbers and documents

Numbers are MASKED (`XXXX XXXX 1234`). `slaDueAt` and `slaRemainingMs` drive the countdown while the submission is pending; `slaHours` is the promise itself, from `RIDER_KYC_SLA_HOURS`. `canResubmit` is false once VERIFIED.

request.description:
**👤 Role:** Rider / delivery partner

**URL:** `GET http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/delivery/wallet`

---

Every money field is INTEGER PAISE. `lowBalance` is computed on the server against `RIDER_LOW_BALANCE_WARN_PAISE` — the client is never asked to hold a second copy of a server-side threshold. `pickFeeMinPaise`/`pickFeeMaxPaise` are the bounds the per-order fee is drawn from, so the app can state the cost honestly before the rider commits. **Auth** — bearer token, role must be `delivery`.

request.description:

**URL:** `POST http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/delivery/wallet/topup/{orderId}/verify`

---

Confirm a top-up from the gateway callback

The same three fields and the same HMAC path as `POST /payments/:orderId/verify`. The amount credited comes from the STORED attempt, never from the request body. Idempotent: a second call on a paid attempt moves no money and reports the same balance.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `delivery`.

**Responses** — `200`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `409`

item.name: [RIDER] Open a gateway order to add money

request.description:
**👤 Role:** Rider / delivery partner

**URL:** `POST http://49.13.70.253:9988/api/v1/delivery/wallet/topup`

---

Open a gateway order to add money

Returns `{ topupId, amountPaise, gatewayOrder }`. Returns 503 `PAYMENT_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED` while Razorpay has no keys — which is the case on this deployment — and writes NOTHING in that case, so there is no orphan attempt and no fabricated success.
